Order Sheet
09/07/2025 Mr. Abhinav Tiwari, counsel for the apppellants.

Mr. Sourabh Gupta, counsel appears on behalf of Mr.
 Sourabh Sharma, counsel for the respondent No.3.
Counsel for the appellants submits that this case may be decided in the Court.
Heard on I.A. No.1/2019, application for condonation of delay of 1364 days' in filing the appeal.

Counsel for the appellants submits that afer passing of the award by the learned Claims Tribunal,
appellants have immediately instructed and handed over the file to their advocate Shri Praveen Kumar Vaishnav, for filing of the appeal before the High Court.
After sometime, they were informed that the appeal has been filed and it will take sometime for its disposal.

When in the month of June,
2019, they approached the office of their advocate Shri Praveen Kumar Vaishnav, they came to know that he died on 20.07.2017 and thereafter, they verified about the status of their appeal, upon which,
they came to know that the same has not been filed.
He contended that the claimants being rustic villagers have relied upon the words of their advocate, engaged to file an appeal before the High Court.
There is no deliberate act on the part of the appellants in causing delay of filing of this appeal.

Mr. Sourabh Gupta, counsel for the respondent No.3 opposing the submission of the counsel for the appellants and would submit that there is an inordinate delay of 1364 days and no sufficient cause has been shown to condone the same.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and the claimants and perused the grounds raised in the application.

The contention of counsel for the appellant is that the brief was handed-over to one advocate Praveen Kumar Vaishnav, who later on died and thereafter, they came to know that their appeal was not filed.

The High Court of Madhya Pradesh in case of Sudama and Others Versus Lalsingh and Others,
reported in 2017 ACJ 315, while considering the long delay of filing in appeal, as observed thus:-

sentences.text: True it is that in filing appeal there is a delay of near about four years, but it is a settled proposition of law that in the Indian culture it is not expected from uneducated villagers or agriculturists or labour class that they are acquainted with the legal procedure, specifically the provision of limitation, to file appeal, and, in such premises, their application for condonation of delay could not be thrown away saying that the same has been filed after a long delay.
In the aforesaid circumstance, this appeal could not be dismissed only on account of filing it at belated stage.

Such aspect was considered by the Apex Court long before while considering the matter of substitution of legal representatives on record at very belated stage, i.e., near about six years in the matter of Ram Sumiran v. D.D.C., 1985 ACJ 569 (SC) and the application was allowed."
"14.

Apart from the aforesaid, I am of the considered view that provision of claim under the Motor Vehicles Act has been enacted keeping in view social welfare of the society at large and under section 173 of the aforesaid Act provision for condoning the delay in filing the appeal has also been provided.

If such law is enacted for welfare of the society at large, then merely on account of delay in filing the appeal, the appeal of a person like the appellants, out of them some were minors, could not be thrown away by dismissing the application under section 5 of the Limitation Act."

Considering the facts of the case and the decision of High Court of Madhya Pradesh, in case of Sudama & Others (supra), in the opinion of this Court, sufficient cause has been shown for condoning the delay of 1364 days.
Accordingly, I.A. No.1/2019 is allowed and the delay of 1364 days in filing the delay is hereby condoned.

Counsel for the appellant further submits that liability to satisfy the amount of compensation is upon the respondent No.3/Insurance Company and it is represented by the counsel, therefore, the case be heard finally at motion stage.
The submission of counsel for the appellant is not disputed by the counsel for the respondent No.3.
With the consent of the parties, matter is heard finally.
Order passed separately.
Signed and dated.

Sd/-
